--- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.set_node_attr_to_display()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | EdgeCase description: Set which node attribute to display in tooltips/labels. twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.set_node_attr_to_display()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | EdgeCase description: Set which node attribute to display in tooltips/labels. title: >- [Graph.set_node_attr_to_display()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: Set which node attribute to display in tooltips/labels. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Set which node attribute to display in tooltips/labels. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L34707-L34793){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.set_node_attr_to_display(attr=None) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Set display attribute](../assets/graphs/set-node-attr-to-display.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="The same six-node graph on both sides, every node carrying a name in a badge (Ann, Bob, Cat, Dan, Eve, Fay). The call changes no node data, so the badges are identical; it only records a display preference, shown as a tag above each graph that reads display: None before and display: name, in the accent color, after." width="100%"} Records the name of a node attribute as the graph's display preference, i.e., the attribute meant to be shown for each node in place of its ID when the graph is rendered. Only this preference is stored; no node data is read, created, or changed, and the attribute name is not validated against the nodes. The call is also logged in the graph's recorded step history. `plot()` uses this attribute for its node text when `label_by=` isn't given. As in `label_by=`, `"label"` and `"id"` are also accepted, and nodes lacking the attribute show their ID. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [attr]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Name of the node attribute to display (e.g., `"label"` or `"name"`). Any string is accepted here; `plot()` raises if no node has that attribute. If `None` (the default), the preference is cleared, which means node IDs are shown. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Self for method chaining. ::: ## See Also {.doc-see-also} [](`~plot`) : Draws the display attribute on each node unless `label_by=` is given. [](`~relabel_nodes`) : Change the labels themselves. ## Examples {.doc-examples} The display attribute is what `plot()` shows on each node when `label_by=` isn't given. It changes no node data, and it returns the graph, so it can sit in a chain: ::: {#0d4c21af .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_node(label="Alice", age=30) .add_node(label="Bob", age=25) .add_edge(source="Alice", target="Bob") .set_node_attr_to_display("age") ) graph.get_node_df() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: Passing `None` clears it, so `plot()` goes back to showing node IDs. ### Departments on the org chart In a small company's reporting lines, each person has a name, a job title and a department. Setting the display attribute once makes every plot show the departments, so it's plain that Sales is the widest team and Engineering the deepest: ::: {#81daf766 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} org = ec.org_chart().set_node_attr_to_display("dept") org.plot(layout="pos", width=820, height=640) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: `label_by=` still wins for a single plot, here going back to the names: ::: {#178be4be .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} org.plot(layout="pos", label_by="label", width=820, height=640) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ```{=html}
